quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead.

questions.question: Using your turn signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other traffic is present.
Is a good habit and is required by law.
Is only necessary during the maneuver, not before.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you change lanes or turn. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train may be near. Obey all railroad crossing signs and never try to go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Where can drivers throw litter while on the road?
questions.explanation: You can only throw trash in a litter barrel on the highway. Litter barrels are found at rest areas and picnic areas. Signs on the road tell you when a litter barrel is ahead.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact with an angry driver. Speeding up may only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When must vehicles have liability insurance?

options.text: Only when driven by a minor.

questions.explanation: All vehicle owners and drivers in Texas must have at least the minimum amount of liability insurance at all times to cover any injury, death, or property damage they may cause.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Use direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What is a sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerking movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop to let them cross safely.
Drive close to scare them so they won't cross against the light again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass, even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance is affected by your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a short break every two hours on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and nap or find a place to stay overnight.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: Traffic signs and road markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and road markings control traffic flow and help guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions instead of the traffic light. Officers direct traffic to keep traffic moving and prevent crashes.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Then quickly glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving into the other lane.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Turns and curves are especially dangerous on slippery roads. Approach them more slowly than you would on dry roads.

questions.question: How should drivers use their cell phones?

options.text: By making calls and sending texts in areas with light traffic.
By using cell phones while driving if you are skilled at it.
By pulling off the road before using the cell phone.
By using cell phones in clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: By pulling off the road before using the cell phone.
questions.explanation: You can use a cell phone to call police or in an emergency. If you must make a call, pull safely off the road. Keep the call short or ask a passenger to make the call if possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. It means that when you turn left at a green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter medicine should:

options.text: Read the label on the medicine before driving.
Keep driving no matter what the label says.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label on the medicine before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive safely. Check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if the medicine is safe to take before driving.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if the area were not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from signs, flaggers, or police in construction zones. Not following these instructions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The driver and all passengers must use safety belts if the vehicle has them. This rule applies to all passengers of any age.

questions.question: When should you drive in a reversible lane showing a red X signal?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic you can see.
If you are passing the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed and if toll booths are open. A red X means that lane is closed. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Increase your distance from the car ahead of you.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see. Take these steps to make night driving safer for you and other drivers.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death in a crash increases. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver should drive through without stopping.
One driver should wave other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The vehicle that arrives first goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: You should slow down in these situations:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.
